api.notes: An ISO 8601 string, or Unix time as a number (seconds, or milliseconds from 10^12 on); the attribute reads a numeric string as a number. An ISO string with no offset reads in the viewer's zone. A value that names no moment renders nothing (and warns in dev).

`relative`, `relative_short`, `auto`, `date`, `date_long`, `date_weekday`, `date_time`, `time`, `system_date`, `system_date_time`, `system_time` or `unix_seconds`; an unknown value warns and reads as `auto`.
Seconds after which `auto` stops being relative.
Inverted: the card is on by default (upstream default true) for relative readings and for any reading with `tooltipEntries`; `no-tooltip` turns it off.

`readonly {timezoneID?, format?, label?, isCopyable?}[]`, one card line each in order. `timezoneID` is an IANA zone, `local` or omitted for the viewer's; an unknown zone falls back to it with a warning. An empty array counts as none.
Appends the zone abbreviation to `date_time` and `time`; never to the `system_*` shapes. Visible text only.
Updates a relative reading as time passes: every second for the first minute, every 30 seconds up to an hour, every minute up to a day, then every five minutes.

api.reason: A-testid: test hooks are the host element and its `::part` names; a `data-testid` attribute on the host is ordinary HTML.

hooks.notes: The copy button writes the line's value, flips to a check for 1.5 s with the tooltip and label "Copied", announces "Copied" politely through the shared announcer, and treats a refused write as a no-op.

keyboard.action: Focuses the `<time>` when it has a card (it is a tab stop only then); focus opens the card.
Closes the card and returns focus to the `<time>` (the hover card's own dismissal).
Activates the focused copy button of a copyable line.

form.notes: Not form-associated: it displays a moment, it does not collect one.

differences.text: `hasTooltip` (default true) is the inverted `no-tooltip`, `isTimezoneShown` is `timezone-shown` and `isLive` is `live`; `value` reads a numeric attribute as Unix time. The card's `open` events stay inside the element (upstream exposes none).

The formatting lives in `@tecton-wc/core/date/instant.js` (`Intl` only; zones through `Intl`, never a date library) and the hover card and the copy buttons load lazily, so a card-less timestamp never pays for the overlay stack; the `<time>` stays visible while they load. "Now" for a relative reading is when the element connected or its value changed, then each live tick.

A relative reading is named by the full date with the zone spelled out (a screen reader would read "PST" as an initialism), and the card's action cells are `<dd>`s so the definition list stays valid. The copy confirmation is a polite announcement, not only a swapped label.

The card is the library's hover card on the Tecton popover fill with a 1px rule; labels use the supporting text role in secondary colour and values the body role in primary colour; the dashed underline marks the reading as interactive.

core.timestamp.notes: Guides: [mwg:coordinate-global-events] an instant is shown per zone as a display choice, the `datetime` is always UTC; [mwg:capture-location-agnostic-data]; [mwg:format-human-readable-durations] relative wording from `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`; [mwg:accessible-web-components] the card on focus, the `<time>` as its tab stop.
